title: BTP and cloud integration for ABAP developers
intro: Focus on what an ABAP developer must design, configure or troubleshoot. Separate the ABAP development model from its hosting location, and distinguish Cloud Foundry app mechanics from the managed ABAP environment.

sources.title: Cloud Foundry: how applications are staged

questions.question: What is BTP and how is ABAP Cloud different?
questions.answer: SAP BTP is a platform of services and environments for applications, integration and related capabilities. ABAP Cloud is a development model with restricted language and released contracts. The managed BTP ABAP environment is one place to use that model; supported S/4HANA editions also provide it.
questions.detail: Explain whether your extension is deployed on the ERP stack or in a separate ABAP environment and how it communicates with the business system.
questions.pitfall: Do not call BTP ABAP simply a normal application container deployed with cf push.

questions.question: How do global accounts subaccounts entitlements and spaces relate?
questions.answer: A global account organizes commercial and administrative scope. Subaccounts separate regional and administrative application contexts. Entitlements allocate permission and quota to consume services. In an enabled Cloud Foundry environment, organizations and spaces structure app and service deployment. These are different layers, not synonyms.
questions.detail: Check the service plan, region, entitlement and required roles before provisioning. The exact provisioning flow depends on the selected service and current account setup.
questions.pitfall: An entitlement is not a runtime container, and every BTP service does not require the same CF-space workflow.

questions.question: What is the difference between IaaS PaaS and SaaS?
questions.answer: IaaS supplies infrastructure, PaaS supplies a managed application platform, and SaaS supplies an application. The key distinction is who operates each part of the stack. In an interview explain your responsibility for code, configuration, identity and data rather than memorizing a provider list.
questions.detail: A managed ABAP environment lets the developer focus on ABAP applications within service constraints; a SaaS business application provides an already implemented business capability.
questions.pitfall: SAP HANA Cloud is a managed database service, not a generic example of a finished business SaaS application.

questions.question: What are a service instance binding and service key?
questions.answer: A service instance is a provisioned service resource. A binding connects an application to that instance and supplies connection material. A service key provides credentials for a supported external client use case. A binding does not universally mean that a separately managed service-key artifact was created.
questions.detail: In Cloud Foundry, binding data is commonly provided through VCAP_SERVICES; other delivery methods exist. Restart or restage as required by the platform and application to consume changes.
questions.pitfall: default-env.json is a local development convention, not the universal Cloud Foundry credential transport.

questions.question: What do containers buildpacks droplets and routes do?
questions.answer: A buildpack supplies language-runtime support during staging, producing a runnable app artifact. Containers isolate running app instances. Routes direct traffic to applications, and multiple instances can serve the same route. Availability also depends on instance count, placement, dependencies and failure behavior.
questions.detail: A blue-green deployment switches traffic between app versions, but schema compatibility and in-flight requests still need a rollout plan.
questions.pitfall: A container is not a standalone virtual machine, and one application does not always mean exactly one container.

questions.question: What do destinations and Cloud Connector solve?
questions.answer: A destination centralizes connection and authentication configuration for a supported consumer. Cloud Connector provides controlled connectivity from the cloud to permitted on-premise resources through its configured tunnel. Both require appropriate identity and authorization; neither makes an unreleased backend API supported.
questions.detail: Trace a failed call through destination configuration, connectivity, exposed resource, certificate or token, and backend permission. Avoid copying credentials into application source.
questions.pitfall: Cloud Connector is not simply an unrestricted inbound opening of the entire corporate network.

questions.question: How do remote transactions differ from local RAP transactions?
questions.answer: A remote API call generally has a separate transaction boundary. A local rollback does not automatically undo a remote commit. Design orchestration with idempotency, explicit statuses, retries and compensation where needed. Do not assume distributed ACID behavior merely because both systems use SAP technology.
questions.detail: If payment creation succeeds remotely but the local response times out, retry with a stable idempotency key or reconcile before creating another payment.
questions.pitfall: Calling HTTP inside an action does not make the remote change part of the local RAP database transaction.

questions.question: What makes event-driven integration reliable?
questions.answer: Publish business events consistently with committed state, use durable delivery where required, handle duplicates and define retry and dead-letter behavior. Consumers should use stable identifiers and be idempotent. Ordering, retention and delivery guarantees depend on the configured broker and protocol.
questions.detail: A workflow starter records the request-event identifier so redelivery does not create a second approval process. Reconcile unprocessed events with business state.
questions.pitfall: Do not promise exactly-once end-to-end processing or global ordering without a specific proven design.

questions.question: Which tools matter to an ABAP developer on BTP?
questions.answer: ADT in Eclipse is the primary ABAP development environment. Fiori tooling such as supported SAP Fiori tools supports UI work. BTP cockpit and service-specific tools manage entitlements, identities, connections and deployment. Use the tool appropriate to the runtime rather than one generic build path.
questions.detail: Know how to establish an ABAP project, find a released API, run ATC and tests, and troubleshoot a service consumer. Check installed tool versions against the target system.
questions.pitfall: The historical name SAP Cloud Platform and a Neo-versus-CF-only diagram are not a complete current BTP model.

questions.question: How would you secure and operate a side-by-side extension?
questions.answer: Use supported authentication, least-privilege authorization and managed credentials. Separate environments, trace requests across systems, monitor latency and failures, and define backup or recovery and deployment procedures. Treat API compatibility and dependency lifecycle as operational responsibilities as well as development concerns.
questions.detail: A production-ready design explains who owns a failing integration, how to replay safely and how to revoke a credential. Include those points in architecture answers.
questions.pitfall: Successful connectivity from a developer machine is not evidence of secure production operation.
